Package com.example.inelasticsearch.cluster

Class ShardRouter

java.lang.Object
com.example.inelasticsearch.cluster.ShardRouter
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public class ShardRouter extends Object implements AutoCloseable
The per-node, per-index storage layer: owns one Lucene IndexService/SearchService pair per shard this node stores (as primary or replica — this class doesn't distinguish between the two, it just knows which shard ids it has local indices for). One ShardRouter exists per index name on a given node (DataNodeServiceImpl keeps a map of them); it does not talk to any other node.

Routing a write is purely local: addDocument(java.lang.String, org.apache.lucene.document.Document) hashes the doc id the same way ClusterTopology.shardFor(java.lang.String) does and rejects it if this node doesn't have a writer for that shard. Nothing here enforces "primary-only writes" — that's a convention the coordinator and DataNodeServiceImpl uphold by only sending direct client writes to a shard's primary; this class will happily accept a write for any shard it owns, which is exactly what replication relies on to apply a replicated write locally on a replica node.

    • ShardRouter

      public ShardRouter(Path baseDir, int totalShards, Set<Integer> ownedShards) throws Exception
      Parameters:
      baseDir - the index's data directory; each owned shard gets a shard-<id> subdirectory holding its own independent Lucene index
      totalShards - the index's total shard count (needed to hash doc ids the same way the rest of the cluster does, even though this node may only own a subset)
      ownedShards - which shard ids to open local Lucene indices for

      Exception

  • Method Details

    • addDocument

      public void addDocument(String id, org.apache.lucene.document.Document doc) throws Exception
      Adds a document to whichever local shard it hashes to. Throws if this node doesn't have a writer open for that shard — callers (the coordinator, or replication) are responsible for only routing here what actually belongs on this node.

      Not visible for search until the next commit() — Lucene readers only see a writer's changes after a commit + reopen.

      Throws:
      Exception

    • commit

      public void commit() throws Exception
      Commits every owned shard's writer and reopens its searcher, so documents added since the last commit become visible to search(org.apache.lucene.search.Query). Called after every write today (no batching of commits across requests), which keeps reads immediately consistent with a node's own writes at the cost of a Lucene commit per request.
      Throws:
      Exception

    • search
